Type is decided by **magic bytes first**, extension second, and the server's `Content-Type`
last. A PNG named `.txt` still renders as an image, and a `Content-Type` of
`application/octet-stream` never overrides a filename that says more.

| Category        | Formats                                          | Engine                      | Fidelity        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------- |
| Images          | png, jpg, gif, webp, avif, svg, bmp, ico, tiff¹  | Native                      | exact           |
| PDF             | pdf                                              | pdf.js                      | exact           |
| Word            | docx, docm                                       | mammoth                     | approximate     |
| Legacy Word     | doc                                              | Built-in OLE2 reader        | text only       |
| PowerPoint      | pptx, pptm                                       | Built-in OOXML reader       | content only    |
| Spreadsheets    | xlsx, xlsm                                       | Built-in OpenXML parser     | values          |
| Legacy sheets   | xls, ods                                         | SheetJS _(you supply it)_   | values          |
| Delimited       | csv, tsv                                         | Built-in RFC 4180 parser    | exact           |
| Markdown        | md, markdown, mdx                                | marked + DOMPurify          | rendered        |
| Code            | 50+ extensions                                   | highlight.js                | highlighted     |
| Structured data | json, jsonl, geojson                             | Built-in                    | pretty-printed  |
| Video           | mp4, webm, mov, ogv²                             | Native                      | exact, streamed |
| Audio           | mp3, wav, ogg, m4a, flac, opus                   | Native                      | exact, streamed |
| Archives        | zip, jar                                         | JSZip                       | file listing    |
| Fonts           | woff, woff2, ttf, otf                            | FontFace                    | live specimen   |

¹ TIFF and HEIC depend on the browser; Safari handles both, Chrome does not.
² `.mkv` and `.avi` are detected but usually cannot be decoded — the error says so explicitly.

Anything unrecognised gets a clean download card rather than a broken view.

## A note on Office fidelity

`.doc`, `.docx` and `.pptx` are converted **in the browser**, so nothing leaves the reader's
machine — but they are not pixel-accurate.

- **Word (`.docx`)** becomes clean semantic HTML: headings, tables, bold and italic, inline
  images. Page geometry, headers and footers, columns and text boxes are dropped.
- **Legacy Word (`.doc`)** is not a zipped XML package but an OLE2 container of binary
  records, so it has its own built-in reader. It recovers **text only** — paragraphs, tables
  and field results, with no formatting. Table structure is inferred from Word's cell marks,
  which is exact for ordinary tables and approximate for merged layouts.
- **PowerPoint (`.pptx`)** gives you text, images and presenter notes, not slide layout,
  theming, animation or SmartArt.

<Aside type="caution" title="When layout matters">
  If the file sits at a **public URL**, the toolbar offers *Open in Microsoft Office viewer*,
  which renders it server-side at full fidelity. That sends the URL to Microsoft, so it is
  always an explicit click — never automatic. Turn it off entirely with
  `configure({ officeViewer: false })`.
</Aside>

## Legacy spreadsheets

Modern `.xlsx` and `.xlsm` work with **zero extra dependencies** — the library includes a
native OpenXML parser that reads cell values, shared strings and dates. Binary `.xls` and
OpenDocument `.ods` are different formats; see
[configuration](/fileon/reference/configuration/#legacy-spreadsheets) to enable them.

## Without a bundler

A single module script is enough. This registers the elements and gives you a working viewer
on a static page.

```html
<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fileon/+esm"></script>

<file-preview src="/report.pdf" bordered></file-preview>
```

## What gets downloaded

The entry is about **17 kB gzipped**. Every viewer beyond that is a separate chunk loaded on
first use, so a page that only ever previews images never downloads pdf.js, mammoth or JSZip.

<Aside type="tip" title="Check it yourself">
  Open the network panel on the [home page](/fileon/) and click through the sample files. Each
  new format pulls exactly one new chunk.
</Aside>

Call `configure()` once at startup. Every key is optional and merges over the defaults.

```js
import { configure } from 'fileon';

configure({
  maxBytes: 100 * 1024 * 1024,   // refuse to buffer anything larger
  maxTextBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024, // truncate text and code past this
  officeViewer: true,            // allow the "Open in Office viewer" action
  credentials: 'same-origin',
  headers: { 'X-Tenant': 'acme' },
  locale: 'en-GB',
});
```

| Option                   | Default            | Purpose                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `maxBytes`               | `100 MB`           | Hard ceiling on buffered files. Media still streams.       |
| `maxTextBytes`           | `5 MB`             | Text and code past this is truncated, never silently.      |
| `officeViewer`           | `true`             | Offer the Microsoft viewer for Office files at public URLs.|
| `headers`                | —                  | Sent with every remote fetch.                              |
| `credentials`            | `'same-origin'`    | Fetch credentials mode.                                    |
| `locale`                 | OS locale          | Number and date formatting in the spreadsheet viewer.      |
| `pdfWorkerSrc`           | CDN                | Where pdf.js loads its worker from.                        |
| `pdfCMapUrl`             | CDN                | pdf.js CMap data.                                          |
| `pdfStandardFontDataUrl` | CDN                | pdf.js standard fonts.                                     |
| `loaders.xlsx`           | `null`             | A SheetJS loader, for `.xls` and `.ods`.                   |

## pdf.js assets

By default pdf.js pulls its worker and font data from a version-pinned CDN, which needs no
setup. If you are **offline, self-hosted, or running a strict CSP**, point it at local copies.
This one line works in Vite, webpack 5 and Rollup:

```js
configure({
  pdfWorkerSrc: new URL('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs', import.meta.url).href,
});
```

For full offline support, also copy `node_modules/pdfjs-dist/standard_fonts/` and `cmaps/`
into your public directory and point at them:

```js
configure({
  pdfStandardFontDataUrl: '/pdfjs/standard_fonts/',
  pdfCMapUrl: '/pdfjs/cmaps/',
});
```

<Aside type="caution">
  Without standard font data, PDFs that rely on Helvetica or Times render with blank text. If
  a PDF looks empty offline, this is almost always why.
</Aside>

## Legacy spreadsheets

`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv` and `.tsv` are parsed natively with no extra dependency. Binary
`.xls` and OpenDocument `.ods` are different formats, and the library deliberately does not
depend on SheetJS — its npm build is frozen at 0.18.5 with unfixed advisories. Supply the
maintained build yourself if you need those formats:

```js
configure({
  loaders: {
    xlsx: () => import('https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/package/xlsx.mjs'),
  },
});
```

Without a loader, `.xls` and `.ods` get a download card and an `UNSUPPORTED` error whose hint
explains exactly this.

The file-preview and file-preview-modal custom elements, their attributes and properties.

Importing the package registers both elements. You never construct
`<file-preview-modal>` yourself — `openPreview()` manages one per document.

## `<file-preview>`

```html
<file-preview
  src="/file.pdf"
  name="Report.pdf"
  type="application/pdf"
  theme="dark"
  toolbar="false"
  download="false"
  bordered
></file-preview>
```

### Attributes

| Attribute  | Values            | Notes                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `src`      | URL               | The file to show                                    |
| `name`     | string            | Overrides the name derived from the URL             |
| `type`     | MIME type         | Overrides the server's `Content-Type`               |
| `theme`    | `light` \| `dark` | Omit to follow the operating system                 |
| `toolbar`  | `false`           | Hides the toolbar entirely                          |
| `download` | `false`           | Hides just the download button                      |
| `bordered` | boolean           | Draws a border and rounds the corners               |

### Properties and methods

```js
const el = document.querySelector('file-preview');

el.file = someBlob;  // assign any accepted input, not just a URL
el.src = '/other.pdf';
el.source;           // the resolved Source once loaded, else null
el.reload();
el.clear();
await el.download();
```

`file` is a property, not an attribute — it accepts `File`, `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer` and
descriptor objects, none of which survive being stringified into HTML.

## Sizing

The element fills its container and honours `--fp-min-height`:

```css
file-preview {
  --fp-min-height: 600px;
}
```

## `openPreview(input, options?)`

Opens the full-screen modal and returns a handle. One modal is reused per document, so calling
it twice never fights over focus.

```js
const handle = openPreview(files, {
  index: 0,                 // which file in a gallery to open on
  theme: 'dark',            // 'light' | 'dark' — omit to follow the OS
  onLoad: ({ source, viewer }) => {},
  onError: ({ source, error }) => {},
  onChange: ({ index, source }) => {},
  onClose: () => {},
});

handle.element; // the <file-preview-modal>
handle.go(2);
handle.close();
```

`openGallery` is an alias that reads better when you are passing an array.

## `renderPreview(target, input, options?)`

Renders inline into an element or a selector, and returns the `<file-preview>` element.

```js
const viewer = renderPreview('#viewer', '/report.pdf', {
  theme: 'dark',
  toolbar: true,
  bordered: true,
  minHeight: '520px',
});

viewer.file = '/another.xlsx'; // swap without re-rendering
```

## What you can pass

Every entry point accepts the same shapes:

| Input              | Example                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| URL string         | `'/report.pdf'`                               |
| `File`             | from an `<input type="file">` or a drop event |
| `Blob`             | `new Blob([bytes], { type: 'application/pdf' })` |
| `ArrayBuffer`      | bytes you already hold                        |
| Data URI           | `'data:application/pdf;base64,…'`             |
| Descriptor object  | see below                                     |
| An array of any    | becomes a gallery                             |

### Descriptor objects

Use one when the URL alone doesn't carry enough: a signed link with no extension, or an
endpoint that needs credentials.

```js
openPreview({
  url: 'https://api.example.com/files/8fa21c',
  name: 'Q3 report.xlsx', // gives the detector an extension to work with
  type: 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  credentials: 'include',
});
```

## Utilities

| Export            | Purpose                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `configure`       | Set library-wide options. See [configuration](/fileon/reference/configuration/). |
| `getConfig`       | Read the current configuration back.                            |
| `registerViewer`  | Add or override a viewer. See [custom viewers](/fileon/reference/custom-viewers/). |
| `listViewers`     | A copy of the registry, for debugging.                          |
| `toSource`        | Normalise any accepted input into a `Source`.                   |
| `describe`        | Run type detection over `{ name, mime, bytes }`.                |
| `formatBytes`     | `1048576` becomes `"1.0 MB"`.                                   |
| `Kind`            | The viewer categories: `IMAGE`, `PDF`, `DOC`, `SHEET` and so on.|
| `PreviewError`    | The error class every failure uses.                             |
Shortcuts in the modal and the inline viewer.

| Key                      | Action                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd>           | Close the modal                                                |
| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Previous and next file in a gallery                           |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd>           | Cycles inside the modal; focus is trapped, and restored on close |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> / <kbd>⌘</kbd> + scroll | Zoom images and PDFs                           |

Focus is moved into the modal when it opens and returned to the element that opened it when it
closes, so keyboard and screen-reader users are never dropped at the top of the document.

## Dark mode

Dark mode follows the operating system. Force it either way with the attribute:

```html
<file-preview src="/report.pdf" theme="dark"></file-preview>
```

## Shadow parts

For structural changes the tokens cannot reach:

```css
file-preview::part(toolbar) {
  border-bottom: 2px solid var(--brand);
}
```

Exposed parts: `toolbar`, `stage`, `content`, `controls`, `backdrop`, `shell`.
